Graduate Programs
The department offers comprehensive Master of Science and Doctor of Philosophy programs in civil engineering. Active research programs are maintained in the areas of enviromental, geotechnical, structural, transportations/materials and water resources engineering, with the goal of integrating graduate study, research, teaching and engineering practice.

Degree programs options
Doctor of Philosophy
The doctorate degree program is a research-oriented curriculum designed to prepare students for advanced research and university-level academic positions in civil engineering, as well as industry. This program requires a minimum of 90 credit hours or 60 credit hours beyond the masterâs degree, including at least 30 hours of research credit. A dissertation of original research of sufficient quality and importance to merit publication in refereed journals should be completed by all doctoral students.
View Ph.D. program details
Master of Science
The masterâs program is a broad-based curriculum designed to prepare students for advanced positions in civil engineering industry, consulting and public agencies, as well as for further graduate studies. Students can choose a thesis or project option, or pursue their degree online.
View master's program details
Accelerated B.S./M.S.
An accelerated B.S./M.S. degree program is available for high-performing students to earn bachelorâs and masterâs degrees with limited overlap of coursework. Students can choose between completing research with thesis or a coursework only option.
Learn more about the accelerated program
Graduate certificates
Students can earn a transportation engineering graduate certificate or geoenvironmental graduate certificate by completing 12 hours of coursework.
Learn more about the certificate programs
